title: PUBG Mobile Rare Skin Screenshots: Verification Checklist
summary: How to review X-Suit, weapon, car-skin and outfit screenshots without mistaking previews for ownership.
intro: PUBG Mobile cosmetic screenshots are easy to misunderstand. Promotional artwork, collection previews, inventory tiles and upgrade-stage panels answer different questions. This checklist helps readers identify what an image actually proves.

sections.heading: Begin by identifying the screen
paragraphs: A polished event banner shows that an item was promoted; it does not establish that a particular account owns it. A collection preview can show locked rewards alongside completed ones. An inventory panel is more relevant, but may still need a clear item name and stage indicator. Determine whether the screenshot came from the player's wardrobe, weapon lab, vehicle collection, event page or social-media graphic. Never infer account ownership solely from a background image, animation or title placed over the screenshot.
points: Check whether the UI visibly says owned, locked or preview.
Read item names instead of relying on similar-looking artwork.

sections.heading: Record the exact cosmetic and its stage
paragraphs: For an X-Suit, note the suit name and upgrade stage if shown. For a weapon finish, note the gun model, cosmetic name, current level and unlocked effects. For a vehicle skin, check the compatible vehicle type and whether the skin is in the collection or simply shown as a redemption reward. A creator may use shorthand such as max, full or rare, but those words should be replaced with observable details. An outfit image alone does not establish that all related accessories or animations are included.
points: Distinguish a base outfit from its separately obtained accessories.
Do not treat a promotional final form as an owned upgrade.

sections.heading: Look for cropping and inconsistent context
paragraphs: Screenshots can omit the top bar, account name, event label or level information. A narrow crop may be useful for showing artwork but unsuitable for verifying claims about quantity or ownership. A collection counter without its category label is similarly ambiguous. Check whether the language, game version and interface design correspond to the claimed date. An edited collage of several screens can illustrate a collection but should not be presented as one unbroken inventory view. When clarity is missing, state that the claim remains unverified.
points: Do not rely on visual compression artifacts alone to allege fraud.
Ask for clear contextual views rather than private account access.

sections.heading: Protect accounts during any verification
paragraphs: A legitimate explanation of cosmetic ownership does not require sharing recovery email access, two-factor codes or device-login approval. Account transfer can violate publisher rules and may involve recovery or penalty risks regardless of screenshot quality. Use information visible to a normal viewer and keep personal identifiers out of public demonstrations when possible. If a shared screenshot reveals payment history, telephone numbers or linked social accounts, redact that information before reposting. Consider the platform's own reporting tools when a listing makes demonstrably false claims.
points: Never share a one-time password to show an inventory.
Remove phone numbers and recovery details from shared screenshots.

sections.heading: Write descriptions that can actually be checked
paragraphs: A helpful cosmetic description uses specific facts: named item, quantity if countable, current upgrade level, and which shown features are unlocked. Separate confirmed inventory items from planned purchases or future event rewards. If the only evidence is a video thumbnail, say so rather than writing a definitive claim. Avoid claims of guaranteed account safety, permanent transfer or exclusive rarity without supporting publisher information. This approach is useful for collectors documenting their own items as well as for readers evaluating pictures posted online.
points: Use neutral wording when evidence remains incomplete.
Update a description when a newer inventory screen resolves the uncertainty.
